Three concurrent fixes after the wedge re-emerged in coupling.py (R1 of
prior wave only fixed modularity.py):

1. Share partition across 3 metrics per env.step. compute_reward now calls
   safe_louvain twice per step (once each for before/after) and passes the
   partition as _partition kwarg to compute_modularity / compute_cohesion /
   compute_coupling. Worst case shrinks from 6 Louvain runs to 2.

2. Memoize safe_louvain by (frozenset(nodes), frozenset(edges)). NOOPs and
   failed refactor ops (graph unchanged) cost zero. Cache key includes
   nodes-frozenset to avoid colliding graphs with identical edge sets
   but different isolated-node sets.

3. Drop WATCHDOG_SECONDS from 1.0 to 0.05. OK seeds run Louvain in
   microseconds so unaffected; wedged topologies short-circuit fast.

4. Extend safe_louvain pattern to coupling.py (was still calling raw
   nx_comm.louvain_communities). cohesion.py already used the shared
   helper.

5. Autouse fixture in tests/unit/services/metrics/conftest.py clears the
   partition memo between tests so monkey-patched watchdog tests stay
   deterministic.

Empirical: seed=123 was 7+h indefinite hang → now 51.3s collect_rollout
(below the 120s isolated-wrapper budget). seed=314 next.

All 64 architecture tests pass, ruff + format clean, file-size cap holds.
